_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for stop-model work across sessions and accounts. Every session reads this first and updates it before ending. Do NOT restate this status in prose anywhere else -- a second copy is how drift starts. `python3 scripts/state.py` renders it as a table AND verifies every `verify` probe below against the real code, failing loudly when a claim and the codebase disagree.
audit_rule: NOTHING counts as done until an adversarial round comes back clean. audit_rounds counts rounds RUN; audit_clean is true only when a round found nothing. A phase with status=shipped and audit_clean=false is NOT finished. This applies to `already_shipped` entries identically -- being written in that list means the CODE is done, never that the WORK is.

phases.name: Piece 4 -- per-position premium stop
phases.note: Built and green. TWO adversarial rounds run, NEITHER clean. Round 1 found 8 defects (all fixed). Round 2 found 8 more in this phase alone, all fixed: the frontend PREMIUM_STOP copied only one of the backend's two guards, so a failed quote (currentPrice coerced to 0) fired a Critical toast for EVERY position on every 30s cycle with no backend alert behind it -- a regression the pnlPct test it replaced did not have; the card displayed one premium stop and posted another, twice over (the reset re-seeds the field without telling the parent cache, and mergePlan swaps `exit` under an overridden card without changing `contract` so nothing re-runs -- the second reproduced the 78% stop that round 1 was supposed to have killed); a dollar stop at or beyond the entry fell back silently and also discarded a valid client-sent fraction; the drawer cleared the override on any entry >= 100 and persisted every keystroke, so typing '45' armed a 4% stop; the server-derived fraction was dropped from the create response, leaving the two engines disagreeing until the next sync; a dead schema field; and two tests that asserted plumbing while claiming to cover behaviour -- the router derivation and the PATCH write had NO test, and now go through the endpoint. NOT YET CLEAN -- round 3 pending. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was the same display-vs-posted split round 2 thought it had closed, reached by REVERSING the order of the two events: an unrelated edit BEFORE a mergePlan caches the old seed, the re-seed effect then moves the field without telling the parent, and premiumStopDollarToSend compared the stale cache against the NEW seed and let it through -- card showing $0.80 while $1.50 was posted. Root cause was inferring touched-ness by comparing values; it is now TRACKED and threaded to the page via onEditsChange's meta.premiumStopTouched, which also fixes the mirror defect (a user who typed the seed's own value back had the choice discarded). Also: the offline-retry path in syncFromBackend dropped the server-derived premiumStopPct, leaving the two engines disagreeing; the auto-trader test asserted the resolver directly and never called fire() or _check_daily_loss, so BOTH call sites could be reverted with 75 tests still green (replaced with two that drive the service and fail on that mutation); entryPrice had no gt=0 so a non-positive entry silently dropped the user's dollar stop unlogged; the drawer rewrote a stored stop on a bare focus-and-blur (0.4843 rendered '48' and committed 0.48) and could not represent sub-1% or >=99.5% fractions at all; and the persisted store gained two fields with no version bump (now v3). ROUND 5 (11 findings, all fixed): the badge percentage came from the printed pair while the badge's COLOUR and tooltip (`status`) still came from full precision, so at a 0.70 pass line $1.77 away x 0.789 on a $2.00 premium printed '70% OF PREMIUM' in PASS green above an equation that hand-checks to exactly 70% (~0.18% of ordinary inputs) -- the verdict now comes from the same printed pair, via one shared printedFrom(); a sub-cent premium produced a card of four contradictory zeroes ('0%' badge, total-loss tooltip, '$0 of $0 premium') and now returns null into the existing N/A path; PremiumStopEditor's two REVERT paths returned without clearing dirtyRef, so typing 100, blurring, then merely clicking in and out PATCHed a live stop nobody touched -- round 4's defect re-entered through the rejected-edit path; lastStoredRef's 'never while the user is mid-edit' was asserted but not implemented (a 30s sync overwrote typing); FastAPI's `detail` is a LIST for a validation 422 and all four parse sites cast it to string, so entryPrice's new gt=0 bound could crash the whole Portfolio page via detail.split(); the card's premium-stop field was min=0.01 with no max, so typing 0 -- the natural way to say 'no override' -- clamped to $0.01 and pinned a 0.19% stop (Critical alert on the first cent of adverse move, and a ~3000x cut to the auto-trader's daily-loss denominator), now bounded to 10-99% of the mid to match the global's own ge=0.10 bound; the router's live-quote guard tested the RAW quote and rounded after, so a $0.004 quote stored entry_price 0.0, which alert_generator's `entry_price > 0` gate makes permanently unable to raise a stop alert; the Alerts page rendered the resolved stop through Math.round, reprinting the exact 0%/100% lossiness premiumStop.ts documents as fixed; and AutoTradeArm's doc comment claimed arming and sending 'cannot arm a position at two different stops' when they share only the DOLLAR by design.

already_shipped.name: Stop-cost notation rework
already_shipped.note: Frontend copy only, no logic change. Round 1 fixed the headline's three independently-rounded figures. ROUND 2 found the equation STILL did not reconcile, in both directions, because `r.capped` is decided at full precision while the line prints a 3dp delta: capped with the product below the premium printed '(uncapped $38.55)' beside '$38.59 of $38.59' -- an uncapped figure BELOW the capped one, impossible by construction; uncapped with the product above printed '= $52.48 of $52.48' where the printed factors give $52.52, with no tail, above a headline claiming '$0 left' for a stop the code did not classify as a total loss. Round 1's own range test could not have caught either: it skipped every capped row and re-implemented the clamp as the expected value. Both now decided on the printed product. Round 2 also found the badge's percentage still came from full precision while the headline came from the printed pair ('100% OF PREMIUM' beside '$8 left'), and that 'of the $X you paid' names a scan-time mid that the editable Limit and the contracts-scaled CaR both contradict. THIRD TIME THIS ITEM HAS SHIPPED A NON-RECONCILING FIGURE. NOT YET CLEAN. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The badge TOOLTIP was the last consumer of full-precision `capped` while the label and headline beside it came from printedShare, so with ordinary 4dp deltas it called a contract a total loss above '99% OF PREMIUM' and '$1 left' ($55.92 x 0.1622 on a $9.07 premium). Now branches on stopLossIsTotalOnPrintedFigures and is pinned by a sweep that fails on the mutation. Separately, the printed product used toFixed(2), which breaks an exact half-cent on the BINARY value: 8.01 x 0.500 = 4.005 printed $4.00 where a hand-check gives $4.01 -- and that is this rework's OWN documented worked example, with three tests pinning the artefact. Rounding is now explicit half-up (roundCents) and the range sweep re-derives the rule independently rather than importing it. ROUND 5: the badge's percentage and its COLOUR were decided at two different precisions (see phase D note) -- fixed at the root so one printed pair drives the verdict, the percentage, the headline and the tooltip. Sub-cent premiums no longer render at all. AND the badge now carries the dollars left, per share, per decision BADGE-SPEC-2026-09-05.

already_shipped.name: Schematic removals -- Invalidation readout + Projected R/R
already_shipped.note: Both approved by Kenneth. (1) The Final Recommendation's standalone invalidation probability -- its no-race fallback -- is gone; the Monte Carlo card's own copy had already moved to the Barrier Race. firstPassage.invalidation and data.exit.invalidation are untouched, so the send gate still fires. (2) The Projected R/R (+8%) readout is gone from the Final Recommendation's Ladder-DEFAULT branch -- the copy that survived its removal from the Ladder section itself, and the one seen first since it is the card's opening state. overlay.premiumStop stays. KNOCK-ON: computeEditedRR, isDirty and the `dirty` memo were deleted as dead, which removes the card-level 'edited' flag (see open question). UNAUDITED. ROUND 1 confirmed every stated invariant of the removals holds, and found two comment defects: one promised a stop the branch does not print, one implied a freshness guarantee scoped only to the race. Both corrected.  ROUND 2 re-checked the orphan sweep independently and confirmed it: isDirty/computeEditedRR had no other callers, data.rrRatio/rrModel are still consumed by the context rail, firstPassage.invalidation still feeds BarrierRaceCard, data.exit.invalidation still hard-blocks the send, and the per-target 'edited' badge survives. Two more comment defects found and fixed: an orphaned JSDoc (the new stopCostShown prop was inserted between `invalidation`'s doc block and `invalidation`, so tooling attributed the standalone-invalidation description to it), and the section header still promising the Ladder-default branch prints 'T1/T2/T3 + R:R' when the R:R is exactly what was removed. NOT YET CLEAN. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. Nothing new wrong with the removals themselves -- no orphaned data, props, types or CSS, and nothing still computed into nothing. Round 3's two observations here are both recorded rather than built: the lost card-level 'edited' flag is already decision EDITED-FLAG-2026-09-04 (REBUILD AS NEW UI, approved, in pending_kenneth), and the badge's departure from the schematic is now an open question below. What WAS missing was coverage: the rendered surface of the rework had none, so the header name the Barrier Race cross-refers to, the per-contract headline, and both directions of stopCostShown are now asserted. ROUND 5: no new defect in the removals themselves -- the auditor re-verified that isDirty/computeEditedRR/dirty/editedRR are gone with no orphans, that data.rrRatio/rrModel remain live via the context rail and tradeCardSnapshotOf, that firstPassage.invalidation still feeds BarrierRaceCard and data.exit.invalidation still hard-blocks send, and that stopCostShown gates the readout and its cross-reference from one expression. Rounds are counted together with the other two items.

The branch may then render nothing until Estimate is clicked, which is accepted -- consistency with how the rest of the card treats stale numbers wins. Pre-existing behaviour, but with the invalidation fallback removed those rows are the only numbers left in the branch. NOT YET BUILT.

decisions.q: SPEC DEVIATION raised by round 3: the schematic's card 03 puts the dollars-left ON the badge and per SHARE ('Caution - 71% of premium - $1.49 left'); what shipped kept the badge percent-only with per-CONTRACT dollars on the headline below. Which?
decisions.a: MATCH THE SCHEMATIC. The badge now reads '<pct>% of premium - $<x.xx>/share left'. Reason it matters beyond this card: the badge is what the ranking view will reuse, and there it would travel with only a percentage -- the half that does not say whether being wrong costs $8 or $800. Two consequences accepted deliberately: (1) the card now shows the same quantity twice in two units a foot apart (per share on the badge, per contract on the headline), so both strings name their unit; (2) '/share' rather than the schematic's bare '$1.49 left' because StatusBadge uppercases its label and is white-space:nowrap -- the CONTENT follows the schematic, the CASING follows the design system. BUILT.

open_questions: Do the Q7 thresholds (0.80/0.70/0.60) hold on a real universe? Round 5 records them as taken as proposed, never measured.
Is Tradier's per-contract IV good enough in production to displace a solver for Phase A?

ivRank is conflated: market.py:1277 writes raw IV x100 into a field named for a percentile, 1291/1308 conditionally overwrite it with a genuine rank, and scan.py:610-616 broadcasts an ATM value across every strike. It is compared against iv_rank_pass_max: 34 and hard_reject.max_iv_rank: 70 -- a LIVE scoring/hard-reject defect, not a tidy-up.

Should the auto-trader's daily-loss gate size on the full premium instead of the premium stop? Since piece 4 the denominator can come from ArmRequest.premium_stop_pct, so a tighter declared stop shrinks premium_at_risk and lets more trades through -- and nothing enforces the declared stop, because the auto-trader places no protective order. Deliberately not clamped. ROUND 5 UPDATE: the reachability was far worse than this text implied -- the card's stop field was min=0.01 with no max, so one keystroke cut the denominator ~3000x via a field whose label says nothing about auto-trade sizing. That field is now bounded to 10-99% of the mid, so the remaining exposure is a deliberate 6x (a 10% stop against the 0.60 default), not a fat-finger. The underlying question -- full premium or declared stop -- stands.

Should a PREMIUM_STOP alert stamp the threshold it fired at? Raised by round 5. The Alerts page resolves the percentage LIVE from the position, so editing a position's stop silently relabels its historical alert rows with a threshold those alerts never used. Stamping at fire time needs a field on the toast, a persisted alertStore migration, and the same field from the backend generator's websocket path -- cross-cutting enough to decide rather than half-do. The lossy Math.round on that label was fixed in round 5; only the vintage question is open.

Record-keeping, not a defect: the schematic's card 03 heads this section 'Stop cost' and states that every other field and line of explanation stays as it reads today. Shipped is 'MAX LOSS IF THE STOP IS HIT', approved as NOTATION-2026-09-04 but never recorded as a departure from the artifact. Confirm the schematic should be amended rather than the header reverted.

traps: migrations/env.py:41 overwrites whatever sqlalchemy.url a caller sets with settings.DATABASE_URL. An alembic test that does not also set the env var silently migrates the real dev database. get_settings() is lru_cached, so clear the cache too.
An earlier migration alters a foreign-key constraint, which SQLite cannot do without batch mode. The chain cannot replay from empty -- stamp one revision back and run only the step under test.
The Barrier Race card renders NOTHING until Run Monte Carlo Estimate is clicked (BarrierRaceCard/index.tsx:119). An invisible card reads as an unshipped one.

Do not trust an audit finding without a file:line you have checked yourself. Session 12 accepted a round-1 finding uncritically and committed its errors; round 2 found four of nine corrections did not survive contact with the code.
A bs_iv test written against the reference contract (215C) alone passes and hides the entire defect.

Run the backend suite as plain `pytest`, with NO DATABASE_URL set. tests/conftest.py:54 does `os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", <isolated test db>)`, so it already isolates the run -- and because it is setdefault, an env var YOU export wins and defeats it. Exporting DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: (advice inherited from the alembic trap above, which applies only to alembic tests) makes tests/test_db_isolation.py fail: 1 failed / 1992 passed with it, all green without it. Round 5 chased that failure to ground -- do not read it as a real regression.

The backend venv is at backend/.venv, not backend/venv, and nothing outside it has pytest or pydantic. Round 5's audit subagent concluded 'pytest and pydantic are not installed in this container' and reported every backend finding as inspection-only. Both backend findings it raised that way turned out real, but tell an auditor the interpreter path (backend/.venv/bin/python) so it can verify rather than guess.
